reading.body:
Expedient's four tracked facilities total 10.6 MW of nameplate capacity but only 5.7 MW of published critical IT load, and the gap is not idle space.

The 10.6 MW figure is a market-level number, not a building-level one. Pittsburgh South carries 6 MW against a building the operator publishes at 1.8 MW, because that 6 MW is the whole Pittsburgh market including a second building, Pittsburgh Central, that the registry does not track as its own row. Owings Mills carries 2.3 MW against a building published at 800 kW, because that is Expedient's Baltimore market figure. Tidepoint carries 2.3 MW against 1.5 MW. Only Milwaukee, at 1.6 MW against 1.6 MW, is a one-to-one match. Anyone reading these numbers as per-building capacity will overstate three of the four.

What the buildings themselves show is a colocation operator sized for enterprise workloads rather than AI training. The largest single critical IT load published anywhere in this data is 1.8 MW at Pittsburgh South. Raised floor runs between 8,800 and 12,000 square feet per site, and on-net carrier counts run from four to six. Standby generation is diesel and exceeds critical load at every facility where both are published, which is the normal shape for a site built to ride out an outage, not to serve a training cluster. No utility service size appears anywhere in the data, so nothing here speaks to how much power these sites could actually draw if they were rebuilt for denser compute.

The data covers four buildings in three states and does not cover the rest of the company. Expedient publishes market pages for Boston, Cleveland, Columbus, Denver, Indianapolis, Memphis and Phoenix that have no rows here, and states an aggregate of 35 MW of critical IT load across more than 472,000 square feet, so the tracked facilities are a minority of the footprint. The Baltimore market is the clearest gap: the operator quotes 2.3 MW and 55,000 square feet for that market while describing only the Owings Mills building, which implies a second Baltimore site the data does not identify. Tidepoint appears in the registry with coordinates in Locust Point but no address tags and no current operator page corroborating it. Wisconsin appears in the facility rows but not in the operator's state list. No year-opened date exists for any of the four buildings, so nothing here supports a claim about when this capacity was built or how fast it has grown.
